title: Export a finished project as a scoring service
request: The challenge's rubric asked for an API with Flask and Gunicorn, Docker and tests. Next to the notebook export, export a finished project as a scoring service that computes the same features as training and holds no data.
spec: A package with the fitted feature builder and model, a Flask app served by Gunicorn (health, model, predict one, many or a CSV), a Dockerfile without data, tests from made-up rows; with the behaviour recipe, a batch's counts added to stored ones. Done when the replica's export builds, its own tests pass, the image runs in the end-to-end flows, and an unapproved project is refused.
plan: Write studio/service.py: refuse a project whose final stage is not approved; refit through runner.fit_and_predict, which now returns the fitted recipe.
Strip the pickle of data: replace the bundle by its spec, drop per-row rates, hash category levels, feature names, entity values and places.
Vendor the code the scorer needs and write app.py, scorer.py, requirements, a Dockerfile copying no data and tests on made-up rows.
Test that the exported scorer, run in a Python that cannot import the repository, gives the engine's predictions, and that no row value is in the export.
Run the export's own tests once in a clean Python 3.12 environment.
Fix the review's findings; mark the package done in part.

decisions.decision: The service computes behaviour features within each request; a single row is told it has no history.
decisions.why: The engine measured the model with features computed within each fold; storing training-period history in the service would make served features differ from the evaluated ones. The stateful service is recorded as open.

decisions.decision: The hashing key is never in the exported folder; the service reads it at serve time (DCLAB_SERVICE_KEY).
decisions.why: A salt pickled next to the hashes lets anyone enumerate phone numbers or grid cells and recover them.

decisions.decision: The export refuses a refit that does not reproduce the approved holdout score.
decisions.why: The served model must be the approved one; a refit that scores differently is a different model.

decisions.decision: The service gives an alert only at a stated budget.
decisions.why: The plan says the threshold is chosen with the person; without a budget the service returns scores.

change: studio/service.py and service_template/ (scorer, Flask app), model.pkl without data, model.json with the training column types, review changes and the threshold, vendored code, Dockerfile and generated tests; dclab_core.behaviour hiding keys with a serve-time key; ECOD keeping a quantile grid; tests/test_service_export.py; the 15.10 acceptance test unmarked.

findings.defect: Replica phone values were in the export.
findings.scenario: The first export test searched the exported files for row values and found a phone value of the replica inside the model files: category levels and entity keys were stored as they were.
findings.cause: The fitted encoders and count tables keep their keys.
findings.fix: Hash category levels, feature names, entity values and place keys; the scorer applies the same hash to its input.

findings.defect: Private values could be recovered from model.pkl, which also went into the deliverables' git repository.
findings.scenario: The salt was pickled next to the hashes: the top levels of the phone columns and about one drop-off cell per training ride, with label-derived rates, could be enumerated (about a billion phone candidates, a few million grid cells). If ECOD was the final family it stored every training value of every feature column.
findings.cause: The key travelled with the data it protects, and ECOD kept its sorted training columns.
findings.fix: The key is supplied at serve time and never written to the folder (it was found once more on the behaviour object and cleared before pickling); ECOD keeps a quantile grid instead of the training values.

findings.defect: The suite failed with an unexpected success.
findings.scenario: The 15.10 acceptance test, marked expectedFailure, only imported the service module; once the module existed, make test and rd-check failed.
findings.cause: The marker was left after the package that passes it was built.
findings.fix: Remove the marker and make the test real: export the approved replica project and check the refusal.

findings.defect: Training and serving computed different behaviour features.
findings.scenario: Scoring one row at a time against the engine's holdout scores: part 1 (event mode) differed by up to 0.25 in score and 4 of 60 alerts flipped; part 2 by up to 0.046. The parity test passed the whole holdout as one request, which hid it.
findings.cause: The service keeps no state, so each request's counts come only from its own rows.
findings.fix: Kept within-request semantics deliberately (see the decision), a single row gets a note that it has no history, and the package is marked done in part with the stateful service open.

findings.defect: A kept review change was lost in the service.
findings.scenario: A regression project whose review kept a log target was fitted on log1p(y), but the scorer returned the raw predictions with no expm1 and no clip, serving log-scale numbers.
findings.cause: The scorer did not know the review's changes.
findings.fix: Write the review operations and the target range into model.json and apply them in the scorer.

findings.defect: Hashing changed the rate of a missing key.
findings.scenario: On rows with no drop-off, place_destination_rate was 0.0189 in the engine and 0.0068 in the service: fit turned NaN into the key 'nan', serving kept NaN, so the row got the prior.
findings.cause: Fit and serve normalised missing keys differently.
findings.fix: Hash the keys as text exactly as fit does.

findings.defect: Column types depended on the batch.
findings.scenario: If one row of a JSON or CSV batch lacked an integer column, pandas made the column float and '3' became '3.0': row 0's account_id one-hot sum was 1.0 in a complete batch and 0.0 otherwise.
findings.cause: The scorer inferred types from each request.
findings.fix: Store the training column types in model.json and cast before encoding and hashing.

findings.defect: The export was a refit that nothing checked against the approved record.
findings.scenario: Two identical runs of the mock challenge recorded part-2 holdout AP 0.254 and 0.504 (2 positives in the holdout); a refit of the approved configuration after run 1 gave 0.504, not the recorded 0.254. The test compared one refit with another.
findings.fix: Refuse the export unless the refit reproduces the recorded holdout metric, and test against the record.

findings.defect: The service gave an alert at a threshold the person never chose.
findings.scenario: It emitted 'alert' at the task assessment's threshold, while the plan says the threshold is chosen with the person.
findings.cause: The threshold was taken whatever its source.
findings.fix: An alert only at a stated budget; otherwise scores.

measurements.name: service parity with the engine
measurements.gate: The service's predictions equal the engine's on the replica's holdout, in a Python that cannot import the repository, with no row value in the export.
measurements.result: Equal within 1e-6 on the fraud replica's holdout scored as one batch; no order id or phone value of the table in the export; the key absent; the refit reproduces the approved holdout AP.

measurements.name: the export's own tests
measurements.gate: The generated tests pass in a clean environment (Done-when of 15.10).
measurements.result: 3 passed in a clean Python 3.12 environment, run once by hand; no repository test runs them.

measurements.name: the Docker image in the end-to-end flows
measurements.gate: The image runs in make product-e2e (Done-when of 15.10).
measurements.result: Not run: Docker was not running on this machine, and product-e2e has no service flow yet.
measurements.next: Build the image and add the flow when Docker is available.

outcome: Done in part: a Flask and Gunicorn service with a Dockerfile and tests, no data or key inside, predictions equal to the engine's, refused for unapproved projects or a refit that does not reproduce the approved score. Open: the stateful service (a batch's counts added to stored ones), the Docker image, and the product-e2e flow.
lessons: Hashing is not anonymisation when the key travels with the hashes and the space of values is small.
A parity test that scores the whole holdout at once hides features that depend on the batch; also score single rows.
Pin training column types in a served model; JSON batches change them silently.
